prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production pixel-art transparent sprite sheet for the existing game Guerra Saltana.
Primary request: Tero-Bomba: a recognizable Uruguayan southern lapwing (tero, Vanellus chilensis) that flies across a side-view artillery battlefield and drops a cartoon torpedo bomb.
Style/medium: chunky detailed 16-bit pixel art, crisp stepped pixels, dark 1-2 pixel outline, earthy muted military palette to match capybara soldiers, small readable silhouettes, no smoothing.
Subject: gray-brown lapwing with white belly, black chest bib, small backward black crest, red eye and thin red beak, long reddish legs tucked in flight. Natural bird, no human hands. Facing RIGHT in all bird frames.
Composition: one square sprite sheet in EXACT 2 columns by 2 rows, equal square cells with generous transparent padding. Top-left: tero in flight wings raised, empty feet. Top-right: same tero same body registration wings down, empty feet. Bottom-left: same tero same registration wings extended level/gliding, empty feet. Bottom-right: one separate cartoon olive-green torpedo bomb pointed DOWN, brass nose, tail fins on top; no bird in this cell. Each subject fully contained and centered in its cell, never overlaps another cell; same bird scale across three frames. Bird occupies roughly 75% cell width. Bomb occupies 24% cell width and 55% cell height.
Scene/backdrop: genuinely transparent alpha background across all empty pixels; no ground, no scenery, no checkerboard drawn.
Text: none.
Constraints: exactly three bird poses and one bomb, four cells only. No labels, cell borders, numbers, shadows outside sprites, watermark, gradients, blur, gore or extra objects.
